item.title: SpO2 Drops to 72%. Do You Carry the Kid Off the Mountain? A High-Altitude Medicine Lesson with 21 Junior-High Students on the Jiaming Lake Trail
item.description:
SpO2 drops to 72%. Do you immediately carry the kid off the mountain? On this Jiaming Lake trip, real data from 21 junior-high students gave me an answer that was the exact opposite of gut instinct.

I'm an ER doctor. On this Jiaming Lake trip, my role was team doctor: I carried a fingertip pulse oximeter/forehead thermometer and a stethoscope, a first-aid waist pack (DS-R7 rescue waist pack), and a handheld first-aid case (DS-R1 model) (packed at the very bottom of my heavy pack), and walked 4 days and 3 nights with 25 junior-high students, sleeping as high as Jiaming Lake Cabin at 3,370 m. Of the 25 kids, 4 didn't go up the mountain; 21 actually made the climb.
